**Donor retention is measured by calculating the percentage of donors from one period who donate again in the next period.**[1][2]

## Basic Calculation

The standard formula is:[2]

**Retention Rate = (Number of Donors Retained ÷ Number of Donors Who Gave Last Year) × 100**

For example, if your organization had 1,200 unique donors in 2023 and 720 of them donated again in 2024, your retention rate would be (720 ÷ 1,200) × 100 = **60%**.[5]

## Key Measurement Principles

To ensure accuracy, follow these rules:[6]

- Count **unique people**, not transactions
- Track the same donor identity across both time periods consistently
- Include all gifts from each donor during the measurement period, not just single transactions

## Segmented Retention Rates

Rather than relying on one blended rate, measure retention by donor category:[6]

- **First-time donor retention:** Of new donors in year one, how many gave again in year two (target above 30%)
- **Repeat donor retention:** Of donors who gave multiple times in year one, how many gave again in year two (target above 65%)
- **Major donor retention:** Of high-value donors ($1,000+), how many returned

This segmentation reveals which donor groups need attention, as blended rates can mask problems in specific segments.[6]

## Implementation

Most donor databases include built-in retention or repeat donor reports that automatically calculate these metrics.[5] Investing in donor management software eliminates manual calculations and allows you to track retention trends over time.[1]
